findings.title: Client-side upload size check hardcoded to 10MB
findings.body: The client-side file size check in `validateUploadedFile` is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB (10MB) instead of using the configured `SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. This is inconsistent with the new server-side behavior in `uploads_controller.rb`, which now allows images larger than `max_image_size_kb` by automatically downsizing them (up to 5 attempts of 80% reduction). If `max_image_size_kb` is set to, e.g., 5MB, the server would accept and downsize images between 5MB and 10MB, but the client rejects them outright. Users will see a misleading 'file too large' error for images that the server would successfully process. The error message also incorrectly displays 10MB as the maximum size regardless of the actual configured limit.

findings.title: 413 error handler hardcodes 10MB limit
findings.body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 (entity too large) error handler is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB (10MB) instead of using `SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. When the server returns a 413 error, the client displays an incorrect maximum size to the user. This also breaks the contract with server-side configuration: if an admin configures `max_image_size_kb` to a different value, the error message shown to users will not match.

findings.title: Duplicate `OptimizedImage.downsize` definition shadows old signature
findings.body:
Two definitions of `self.downsize` exist in the same class:
1. `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145
2. `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149

In Ruby, redefining a method completely replaces the previous definition. The second definition shadows the first, making lines 145-147 unreachable dead code. This is an API break for any existing callers that use the old 4-positional-arg signature (e.g., `OptimizedImage.downsize("a.png", "b.png", 800, 600)`): such calls will fail because the 3rd positional argument is now interpreted as a dimensions string rather than width, and the 4th as `opts`. The dead code should be removed to avoid confusion, and callers of the old signature should be updated.

findings.title: `OptimizedImage.optimize` signature change is a silent API break
findings.body: The `self.optimize` method signature changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts={})` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. External callers (plugins, other parts of the codebase) using the old 5-positional-arg signature will silently misbehave: the 4th argument is now treated as a dimensions string (e.g., `800` instead of `"800x600"`), and the 5th argument (previously `height`) is now interpreted as `opts`. There is no deprecation or compatibility shim.

findings.title: Removed `OptimizedImage.dimensions` helper without checking external callers
findings.body: The `self.dimensions(width, height)` public class method was removed as part of this PR. Although it was only used internally by the old `optimize` method, it was a public class method (no `private` declaration) and could be used by plugins or external code. Its removal without a compatibility shim is a potential API break.

findings.title: No tests for new automatic downsizing feature
findings.body: The PR introduces a new automatic downsizing loop in `create_upload` (up to 5 attempts of 80% reduction) and modifies the `OptimizedImage.downsize` and `OptimizedImage.optimize` signatures, but no tests are included. Coverage is missing for: the downsizing loop terminating correctly when the file becomes small enough; the 5-attempt cap being respected; correct handling when `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (e.g., unsupported format); behavior when `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` is 0 (disabled); and that the uploaded file's recorded size matches the downsized result.

findings.title: Same path used for input and output of `OptimizedImage.downsize`
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` is called with identical source and destination paths. While ImageMagick's `convert` typically reads the full input before writing, this is fragile: if a future implementation streams input/output, or if a tool reads the destination file as part of processing, data corruption could occur. A safer pattern is to write to a sibling temp file and then atomically replace.
